title.official: Subsequent encumbrancers not parties in foreclosure action

operative_text.controlling:
3.77   A plaintiff in a foreclosure action must not make any
subsequent encumbrancer a party to the claim unless possession is
claimed from the subsequent encumbrancer.

BOOK_A.title: Subsequent Encumbrancers Not Parties in Foreclosure Action
BOOK_A.related_provisions: 3.41 (no defence in foreclosure);6.5 (notice in foreclosure actions); Part 9, Div.5 (foreclosure rules);11.23 (address for service in foreclosure)
BOOK_A.commentary:
Alberta (unlike some other provinces) postpones questions of subsequent encumbrancers in a foreclosure suit, and they are not ordinarily to be made parties. The subsequent encumbrancer avoids the limitation period by riding the first mortgagee's coattails in its foreclosure suit, and though

a limitation could then be pled by the mortgagor, the time likely would not have expired when the main statement of claim was issued, and time could have been extended by acknowledgment. For foreclosure and summary judgment, the limitation period may bar action on a mortgage by a deemed transferee of it who has paid it off.Part payment and acknowledgment of debt does not suspend time, if the person so acting is not the mortgagee then and could not enforce it then.

Ontario courts had held that general privacy legislation barred one mortgagee from giving a mortgage statement to another mortgagee of the same property, despite the latter's right to redeem that other mortgage!The Supreme Court of Canada reversed. The plaintiff mortgagee does not fully control a foreclosure suit, as every encumbrancer's

claim is also to be considered and adjudicated, and the court has discretion over the remedy which the mortgagee gets, and the court has certain leanings, especially if there is equity in the property, and there are special rules for when and how the mortgagee may buy the property.A writ-holder may be given control of the same or foreclosure proceeding. A mortgage covenant giving up possession is illegal, and so even after a closed, court-

approved sale, the mortgagee cannot change the locks.

BOOK_B.title: Subsequent encumbrancers not parties in foreclosure action

commentary.text: Rule 3.77—Subsequent encumbrancer See Alberta Rules of Court, Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.77. In Caplink Financial Corp. v. Petra Corp., 2015 ABCA 55, the Court explained the origin of Rule 3.77: 24 The nature of foreclosure proceedings in Alberta was recently discussed and reiterated by this Court in Community Futures Lesser Slave Lake Region v. Alberta Indian Investment Corporation, 2014 ABCA 232 (Community Futures). It should be noted that this court's decision was handed down after the appellants' factums had been filed in this appeal. 25 In its judgment, this Court referred to its earlier decision in Canadian Pacific R. Co. v. Canadian Wheat Growing Co. (1919), 47 D.L.R. 102 at para. 3, a unanimous judgment of this Court which made clear that: Our practice in mortgage actions differs materially from the practice in other jurisdictions where subsequent encumbrancers, if not made parties originally, are required to be served with a notice of the judgment or order and thereupon to come in and prove their claims and have their priorities settled. With us, the intention is to postpone all such questions until it can be seen whether there is likely to be a fund by which any of them can benefit. … [emphasis added] 26 When this Court rendered its decision in Canadian Pacific, it did so on the context of the then rule 46 of the Alberta Rules of Court, 1914 which provided: A mortgagee suing for sale or foreclosure with or without other relief shall not make any subsequent encumbrancer a party to the action except for the purpose of obtaining possession against a subsequent encumbrancer actually in possession of the mortgaged property, but all subsequent encumbrancers shall be served with notice of the judgment or order directed or made in the action. 27 Rule 3.77 of the new Alberta Rules of Court is similar …. Old R. 687 read: 687. A mortgagee suing for sale or foreclosure with or without other relief shall not make any subsequent encumbrancer a party to the action except for the purpose of obtaining possession against a subsequent encumbrancer actually in possession of the mortgaged property; but all subsequent encumbrancers shall be served with notice of the judgment or order directed or made in the action. 1. Definition of “Subsequent Encumbrancer” … a “subsequent” encumbrancer is one who is subsequent in time. Preston Construction Ltd. v. Resteel Consultants Ltd. (1980), 32 A.R. 114 (Master), at 127, per Master Funduk. 2. Charge against Land Required I prefer the view that an “encumbrancer” under Rule 687 is one who has a charge against the lands. I am also of the view that, for the purpose of Rule 687, a subsequent encumbrancer must be one who is shown as an encumbrancer on the records of the Land Titles office. Preston Construction Ltd. v. Resteel Consultants Ltd., supra, at 128. 3. Interest in Land Inadequate In my view, a subsequent encumbrancer is a person who is firstly subsequent in time and secondly a person who merely has a charge on the land. A person who has an interest in the land is not an encumbrancer within the context of Rules 687 and 688. Wasyl Holdings Ltd. v. Allarie (1981), 31 A.R. 275 (Master), at 298, per Master Funduk.
